name: Qualtrics
tagline: Enterprise survey and experience management platform for customer, employee, product and brand research.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified.

verdictSummary: The visible part of Qualtrics, a form builder with skip logic and a results dashboard, is genuinely a weekend project. The part people actually buy is everything wrapped around it: signed DPAs, HIPAA and FedRAMP-adjacent paperwork, SSO into an HR directory, panel sourcing when you need 2,000 verified respondents by Friday, and a legal department that already approved the vendor. An org running employee engagement or regulated patient surveys cannot hand that to a self-hosted SQLite app, no matter how clean the code is. If you personally just need to ask people questions and see the answers, build it and never look back. If you need the survey to be defensible in an audit or a board deck, you are paying.
coreLoopDIY: A self-hosted survey builder with branching logic, a public response link, and CSV plus chart output of the results.
requirements: A machine or small VPS to host it
A domain if you want respondents to trust the link
Optional SMTP credentials if you want to email invites
whatYouLose: Respondent panels: Qualtrics can sell you a sample that matches a quota, you cannot
Compliance armor: HIPAA, GDPR tooling, SOC 2, data residency, audit logs, the whole procurement checklist
Enterprise plumbing: SAML SSO, HRIS syncs, Salesforce and ServiceNow write-backs, ticket triggers
Serious statistics and text analytics: driver analysis, weighting, sentiment scoring on thousands of open responses
Deliverability and scale: sending 50,000 invites without landing in spam is its own product
moatNotes: Survey software is a commodity. Survey software your legal, security and IR teams have all already signed off on is not.
whyPeopleStillPay: Nobody buys Qualtrics because the question editor is magical. They buy it because a VP needs employee engagement data that HR and legal will accept, because the results have to flow into Workday or Salesforce without a human touching a CSV, and because when someone asks where the respondent data lives, there is a document that answers. The switching cost is not the questions, it is the historical benchmarks, the dashboards executives already read, and the integrations quietly running in the background. A personal replacement solves the 5 percent of the product that is a form.
notes: The form is a weekend; the procurement approval is not. The moat is compliance paperwork, enterprise integrations and the fact that someone else's legal team already said yes.
prompt:
Build a self-hosted survey tool called "Askbox". Single Next.js app, App Router, TypeScript, Tailwind. Data in SQLite via better-sqlite3, one file at ./data/askbox.db, migrations run on boot. No external services, no telemetry, no accounts system beyond a single admin password read from ADMIN_PASSWORD in .env.

Admin side, behind a cookie session gated by that one password:
- Survey list: create, rename, duplicate, archive, delete.
- Survey editor: ordered list of questions, drag to reorder. Question types: short text, long text, single choice, multi choice, 1-5 and 1-10 scales, NPS (0-10), yes/no, dropdown, email.
- Per question: required toggle, help text, optional randomize choice order.
- Skip logic: per question, rules of the form "if answer to Q3 is X, jump to Q7 or end survey". Keep it simple, evaluate server-side on submit of each page.
- Pages: questions can be grouped into pages, one page per screen for respondents.
- Publish toggle, plus an optional close date and a max response cap.

Respondent side:
- Public route /s/[slug], no login, mobile-first, one page at a time, progress bar, browser-local partial save so a refresh does not lose answers.
- Anonymous by default. Store submitted_at, user agent, and a truncated IP hash only, and say so on the form.

Results:
- Per survey dashboard: response count, completion rate, per question summaries. Bar charts for choice questions, mean and distribution for scales, NPS score computed properly (promoters minus detractors), scrollable list for text answers.
- Charts with a tiny inline SVG component or Recharts, no chart SaaS.
- CSV export, one row per response, one column per question, plus a JSON export.

In scope: everything above, seed script that creates one demo survey with 20 fake responses, README with setup in under ten lines.
Out of scope: multi-user teams, SSO, email sending, panels, translations, webhooks, text analytics, weighting. Do not stub them; leave them out.
Ship a working `npm run dev` and `npm run build` with no type errors.
